title: How big is each part on a line from five to ten?
description: A number line from 5 to 10 is cut into ten equal parts, and three boxes are read by finding the size of one part first. Keeko doubts the part size and thinks every part is 0.1.
teaching_notes: One idea: the size of a part is the length of the line divided by the number of parts. Watch for students who always use one tenth for ten parts.

source: On a line from 5 to 10 cut into 10 equal parts, the box b is
video_script.why: The child has cut gaps of one unit into ten parts and now meets a longer line with ten parts.
video_script.substitution: Find the length of the line, divide it by the number of parts, and count parts from the left end.
video_script.anchor: the number line from 5 to 10 in the book, cut into ten equal parts, with the boxes eigh, b and c
video_script.wrong_answer: each part is zero point one
video_script.wrong_move: Says each part is 0.1 because the line is cut into ten parts.
video_script.payoff_line: Part size is the length divided by the number of parts

final_answer.spoken: the box eigh is six, the box b is seven point five and the box c is nine point five

maths_rules: part size 5 / 10 = 0.5, so two parts make one unit
video_script.design: One number line from 5 to 10 with ten equal parts stays all video. The boxes eigh, b and c sit above the 2nd, 5th and 9th marks.

beats.on_screen: title card From your book; a number line from 5 to 10 cut into 10 equal parts with three boxes above it

marks.scene: the title card arrives and the line is drawn

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about a number line.
<bookmark mark='box'/>The line runs from five to ten, in ten equal parts.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Three boxes sit on it. What decimal does each box stand for?

beats.on_screen: the number line with its three boxes stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the end of the number line

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: length of a line = right end - left end; part size = length / number of equal parts

marks.len: the right end minus the left end is shown
marks.part: the line is cut into equal parts and one part glows

narration: <bookmark mark='len'/>The length of a line is its right end minus its left end.
<bookmark mark='part'/>Equal parts share that length, so one part is the length divided by the number of parts.

beats.on_screen: Given: a line from 5 to 10 in 10 equal parts; box eigh at the 2nd mark, b at the 5th, c at the 9th

marks.given: the line and its ten parts are written
marks.boxes: the position of each box is written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, a line from five to ten in ten equal parts.
<bookmark mark='boxes'/>The box eigh is at the second mark. The box b is at the fifth, and c is at the ninth.

beats.on_screen: To find: the decimal in each box
narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the decimal in each box.
<bookmark mark='len'/>Step one, find the length of the line. It is ten minus five.
<bookmark mark='five'/>The line is five units long.

marks.size: five divided by ten is written
marks.unit: two parts are joined into one unit

narration: <bookmark mark='size'/>Step two, divide the length by the number of parts. Five divided by ten is zero point five.
<bookmark mark='unit'/>Every two parts make one unit.

marks.b: five parts of zero point five are added to five
marks.a: two parts of zero point five are added to five

narration: <bookmark mark='b'/>Step three, the box b is five parts after five. Five parts of zero point five make two point five.
<bookmark mark='b2'/>Five plus two point five gives seven point five.
<bookmark mark='a'/>The box eigh is two parts after five. Two parts make one, and five plus one is six.

marks.c: nine parts of zero point five are added to five

narration: <bookmark mark='c'/>Step four, the box c is nine parts after five. Nine parts of zero point five make four point five.
<bookmark mark='c2'/>Five plus four point five gives nine point five.

marks.vals: the three readings sit in their boxes

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Part size is the length divided by the number of parts.
<bookmark mark='vals'/>The box eigh is six. The box b is seven point five, and the box c is nine point five.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the number line
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: a speech bubble: each part = 0.1; ten parts of 0.1 reach only 6; the bubble is crossed out

marks.fix: ten parts of zero point one stop at six
marks.size: the line is longer than that

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks each part is zero point one, as on the earlier lines.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But ten parts of zero point one reach only six, and this line ends at ten.
<bookmark mark='size'/>The size of a part depends on the length of the line.
